$schema: AX.W62 disposition register — machine-readable BOOK/ARCHIVED/RETIRED rows + their named triggers.
doc: A deferral with a named trigger is only honest if a gate RE-EVALUATES the trigger each close. proof:disposition-live parses this file and FAILS the close if a book/archived row's trigger now re-evaluates MET (e.g. a ≥2-consumer threshold the constellation now crosses) while the row is still booked. The chronic it kills: the native-drawer ≥2-consumer trigger was MET at AT and rode BOOK'd five tranches; the AN ARCHIVED-on-2-consumer-gate items were write-once-watch-never. A trigger of kind 'min-consumers' is MET when at least n DISTINCT present consumer repos (constellation.presentConsumers, self excluded) contain a line matching the grep pattern. AY.W-CARRY onboards the full AT W0-L4 ledger BOOK set + the G-4/5/6 AX-promised rows so the register is the ledger's machine MIRROR; the register-COMPLETENESS clause (proof-disposition-live.mjs) cross-checks every docs/tranches/AY/audit/deferred-ledger-manifest.json bookId against this items set. A 'retired' row is coverage-satisfying but NOT trigger-evaluated (it carries a 'successor' field naming its exact destination).

selfTest.comment: A synthetic always-MET book row the gate evaluates every run to prove its detector is load-bearing: every present consumer imports @mkbabb/glass-ui, so n:1 is trivially met. If the detector does NOT classify this as a violation, the gate is broken and reds loudly (the acceptance-is-the-inverse contract).

The FOUNDING chronic (AY.W-NDA): trigger met-in-prose at AT, rode BOOK'd five tranches before this gate existed; now a watched WATCH row that REDs the instant a 2nd consumer imports dialog-native.
